$comment: Keyword taxonomy and query families for X/Twitter discovery. Editable without touching pipeline code. Operator support was measured, not assumed — see docs/automation/TWITTER_QUERY_STRATEGY.md and probe run 30155078770.

syntax.notes: 788-char query accepted without error. Pagination returns 20 tweets/page. queryType Latest|Top.

clusters.$comment: Reusable term groups. Templates below combine them; the builder quotes multi-word terms and joins with OR.

negative.$comment: Applied conservatively. These are unambiguous non-mathematical senses of 'proof'. Deliberately does NOT exclude generic words like exercise/problem/homework — the Gemini relevance classifier handles those far better than keyword exclusion, which would kill real signal.

clusters.$systemsProvenance: Seeded by hand, then reconciled against the `model` field of data/results.json on 2026-07-25 — that reconciliation added Fable, MathDyad, Rethlas, Archon and Harmonic, whose absence caused a gold-set dispute post to be missed entirely. Re-run `python -m scripts.automation.calibrate` after adding a new system.

defaults.$excludeRetweetsComment: Verified supported. Filtering at the API saves quota; the ingest layer still collapses retweets onto their original as a second line of defence.

3.$comment: Capped hardest and monitored for noise; never creates a candidate on its own.

families.purpose: Explicit claims that an AI system solved, proved or disproved a mathematical problem.
Authors announcing their own result in normal academic phrasing, without the word 'breakthrough'.
families.calibrationNote: Rebuilt after calibration: the original literal listed only generic AI words and therefore missed 'suggested by output from GPT-5.4 Pro'. System names are now in scope.

families.purpose: Formal Lean/Coq/Isabelle verification of an AI-produced result — the strongest corroboration signal we can search for.

Claims that a prior result was wrong, withdrawn, overstated, a rediscovery, or already in the literature. This project's two disputed records (Röll, Graffiti 154) are exactly this signal, and Sprint 1 could not find them at all.
Posts naming a canonical problem registry — these carry deterministic identifiers, so they are the highest-value observations we can collect.
Preprint/repository announcements — evidence for a claim rather than the claim itself.
Posts that actually link arXiv, using the verified url: operator. High corroboration rate by construction.
families.literal: url:arxiv.org (conjecture OR theorem OR "open problem" OR counterexample) (AI OR LLM OR "language model")

families.purpose: Named theorem-proving systems combined with mathematical language. Never a bare model name.
Safety net for wording the taxonomy does not anticipate. Hard-capped, monitored, and never sufficient on its own to create a candidate.

trustedAccounts.$comment: Only handles VERIFIED by the from: probe are enabled. Handles that returned no results are listed disabled rather than deleted, so the record shows they were considered and not silently invented. Never enable a handle that has not been probe-verified.
trustedAccounts.queryTemplate: from:{handle} (proof OR conjecture OR theorem OR "open problem" OR Lean OR counterexample OR formalization)
